evals.prompt: I just got a YubiKey 5 NFC. I want to use it for sudo on Ubuntu 22.04. How do I set this up from scratch?
evals.expected_output: Response must cover: (1) udev rules — both 69-yubikey.rules and 70-u2f.rules with file content or paths, (2) plugdev group membership, (3) pamu2fcfg registration command to generate key mapping, (4) /etc/pam.d/sudo edit showing pam_u2f.so line with authfile=/etc/u2f_mappings, (5) safety warning about keeping a root terminal open during PAM changes, (6) package install (libpam-u2f pamu2fcfg). Should use caveman style in prose.

assertions.name: mentions_udev_rules
assertions.text: Response includes reference to both udev rule files (69-yubikey.rules and 70-u2f.rules) or /etc/udev/rules.d/

assertions.name: includes_pamu2fcfg
assertions.text: Response includes pamu2fcfg command for registering the key

assertions.name: shows_pam_sudo_config
assertions.text: Response shows /etc/pam.d/sudo with pam_u2f.so on the same line or in a code block

assertions.name: mentions_authfile
assertions.text: Response mentions authfile option or /etc/u2f_mappings or ~/.config/Yubico/u2f_keys

assertions.name: includes_safety_warning
assertions.text: Response warns about keeping a root terminal/session open before editing PAM, or mentions risk of lockout

assertions.name: mentions_plugdev
assertions.text: Response mentions plugdev group or usermod -aG plugdev

evals.prompt: How do I use my YubiKey for SSH authentication using PIV certificates on Fedora? I want to generate a key on the device and use it for SSH without a software key file.
evals.expected_output: Response must cover: (1) pcscd install and enable on Fedora (dnf install pcsc-lite, systemctl enable --now pcscd), (2) yubico-piv-tool key generation in slot 9a (yubico-piv-tool -agenerate -s9a -AECCP256 -k), (3) warning to change default PIN 123456, (4) CSR or self-signed cert step, (5) SSH connection via PKCS#11 (ssh -I libykcs11.so or PKCS11Provider in ~/.ssh/config), (6) how to export public key for authorized_keys. Should read piv-management.md reference.

assertions.name: mentions_pcscd
assertions.text: Response includes pcscd installation or systemctl enable/start pcscd

assertions.name: shows_key_generation
assertions.text: Response includes yubico-piv-tool with -agenerate and -s9a flags

assertions.name: shows_ssh_pkcs11
assertions.text: Response includes PKCS11Provider or ssh -I with libykcs11.so

assertions.name: mentions_default_pin
assertions.text: Response mentions default PIN 123456 and urges changing it

assertions.name: covers_cert_or_csr
assertions.text: Response covers certificate creation: either -aselfsign or -arequest (CSR) step

assertions.name: shows_public_key_export
assertions.text: Response shows how to get the public key for authorized_keys (ssh-keygen -D or similar)

evals.prompt: I want to store my TOTP codes (like Google Authenticator / 2FA codes for GitHub, AWS, etc.) on my YubiKey 5 and generate them from the Linux command line. How do I set this up?
evals.expected_output: Response must cover: (1) ykman oath applet (not OTP slot — they are different), (2) ykman oath accounts add -t for TOTP, (3) ykman oath accounts code to generate codes, (4) importing via otpauth:// URI with ykman oath accounts uri, (5) pcscd requirement (CCID/smart card interface), (6) optional: touch requirement -T flag, password protection. Should clearly distinguish OATH/TOTP (stored on smart card, better) from OTP slot (keyboard output, different thing).

assertions.name: uses_ykman_oath
assertions.text: Response uses 'ykman oath' subcommand — not OTP slot or ykman otp

assertions.name: shows_add_totp
assertions.text: Response shows ykman oath accounts add with -t flag for TOTP

assertions.name: shows_code_generation
assertions.text: Response shows ykman oath accounts code command for generating TOTP codes

assertions.name: mentions_uri_import
assertions.text: Response mentions URI import (accounts uri command or otpauth:// format)

assertions.name: mentions_pcscd_requirement
assertions.text: Response mentions pcscd, CCID, or smart card interface requirement for OATH
